svg.text: INSIDE THE SERVER — one turn, start to finish
Drawn from ai/engine: flow.py · extract.py · eligibility.py · recommend.py. Short version of what each stage does.
AUDIO ARRIVES — from any of the three bridges
1 · SPEECH → TEXT
Two engines, one falls back to the other
SARVAM saaras — cloud, paid, best on a bad line
VOSK — offline, free, 80 MB, runs on the box
Sarvam returns 429 or takes over 2 s → Vosk answers
and the call carries on. Measured, not assumed.
Measured on a simulated phone line
clean bad line (noise+loss)
Vosk WER 2% 36%
Sarvam WER 3% 11%
Answers understood: Vosk 68% · Sarvam 89%
Both well inside the 1.8 s turn budget.
n-best text
2 · UNDERSTAND THE ANSWER — cheapest first, stop when one fires
Rung 0
KEYPAD / TAP
free · instant · never wrong
Rung 1
LEXICON — sounds-like match on trade words
~70% of answers · ~5 ms
Rung 2
REGEX — numbers, class levels, years
~2 ms · Q1 and Q2-years
Rung 3
LLM — only 'which of these options?'
uncommon · 400-1200 ms
Rung 4
ASK HER TO CONFIRM — spoken readback
catches what the rest got wrong
HOW SURE IS IT? 0.85 and above → confirm and move on · 0.55 to 0.85 → read it back to her first · below 0.55 → ask again
Two spoken tries, then the keypad menu twice, then DEFER — move on and come back. The call never ends because we could not understand her.
one confirmed field
3 · THE CORE — three parts, in this order
3a · INTERVIEW — seven questions, fixed order, never an agent
language → q0 village → CONSENT → q1 school → q2 family trade → q2 years → q3 what she earns from
→ q4 what she wants to learn → q5 how far / any constraint → q6 own work or a job → q7 local demand
→ READ ALL SEVEN BACK → recommend
q5 may branch to a guardian check — on decisional capacity, never on disability.
PRESS # AT ANY TIME → a real person calls her back. Nobody is trapped in a menu.
3b · ELIGIBILITY GATE — rules only, no model
Her schooling and her years of work, against the
NSQF entry table. Three answers, always:
ELIGIBLE she can enrol today
NEAR-MISS with the exact gap —
'one more year', or 'do Level 2 first'
INELIGIBLE and why
881 expired courses are never ranked.
3c · RECOMMENDER — ranks inside the eligible set only
Scores on written-down, versioned weights:
what she wants · what she can already do ·
local demand · own-work vs job · distance
Returns TOP 3, and the rules that keep it honest:
at most 2 from any one sector
no duplicate titles
plus the best NEAR-MISS
1,198 of 2,814 are actually recommendable.
WRITTEN WITH EVERY RECOMMENDATION: the answers used, the weights version, the engine version, the register's sha256.
In 2030 'why was she sent to this trade' has to be answerable from a row.
4 · WHAT COMES BACK
TO HER — spoken, on the same channel, under a minute
'You have done twelve years of weaving. For this
course you do not need a school certificate.'
· the three options, one plain sentence each
· the near-miss and exactly what would close it
· PM-DAKSH instead, if that fits her better
· ₹50,000 help if she starts her own work
· what to do on Monday, and where
· press 9 to hear it again, any time
TO THE DATABASE — and from there, the officer
answers · consent · the recommendation · outcome
Rolls up to: demand by block and trade,
the Perspective Plan, the consent register,
placement tracking.
Adapters never write here. Only the core does.
5 · AFTER THE RECOMMENDATION — the part that was missing
A recommendation she cannot act on is the CAG's 41% placement figure being made one call at a time.
The interview ending is not the product ending — so every channel has a next step, and somebody is told to follow up.
ON THE CALL
Straight after the three options:
'Shall I send this to you on WhatsApp?'
→ 1 yes · 2 no
'Should the village worker come and
help you enrol?'
→ 1 yes → she is added to the
worker's call list
'Press 9 to hear it again.'
Press # at any time for a human.
IN THE APP — MY PLAN
The plan stays. She can open it any day.
· the three options and the gap, spoken
again on a tap
· what to carry: Aadhaar, caste
certificate, bank passbook, photo
· nearest centre and how far
· 'I WANT TO ENROL' → tells the worker
· a reminder before the batch starts
AND THEN, MONTHS LATER
The worker updates one list on her phone:
RECOMMENDED → ENROLLED → CERTIFIED
→ PLACED (or DROPPED, and why)
Not a new officer screen — the list she
already works from.
This is Basic Issue 3, and the only way
the district learns whether any of it
actually worked.
AND IT LOOPS BACK: a NEAR-MISS is not a rejection. 'One more year' or 'do the Level 2 course first' becomes a task on the
worker's list too — so the same person is re-interviewed when the gap closes, instead of being counted as a failure.
